propositions: An errored side of a paired parity run is incorrectly counted as a decision flip because parity.py:107 compares decision fields without checking the errored flag, scoring a synthetic decision as a model verdict.

A single transient error (e.g. throttling exception) on one arm fails the parity slot as a quality regression under criterion (b) even though errors are already gated separately under criterion (d), causing double-counting.

The parity report cannot distinguish between real decision flips and fabricated flips caused by errors, because errored_pairs is not surfaced in ParityReport.metrics and the gating-failure string does not disclose which flips are erroneous.
An errored record with errored=True and valid=True produces a completely silent fabricated flip with no corroborating signal in error_rate or validity metrics.

The fix excludes pairs where either side has errored=True from decision_flips computation and adds errored_pairs to metrics, guarding on the errored flag rather than decision-vocabulary membership tests.

The recorded live run re-scores identically after the fix with errored_pairs=0 on both slots, confirming the change does not alter verdict on clean data where errors occurred on both arms with identical synthetic decisions.
